# derived from monero v0.18.5.1 source, not captured from a run
# The /proc formats are the kernel's and the check is DESIGN.md §7.1's; nothing was captured.
# Expectation for `ports_owned` against input/. See tests/fixtures/doctor/ports_owned/expect.json for
# the /proc/net/tcp column traps (hex IP in inet_addr order, HEX PORT, st 0A, inode join) and the
# dangling-symlink note.
#
# THIS CASE: 18081 IS HELD BY SOMEBODY ELSE. inode 7701 -> pid 8421, whose argv is
# `/usr/bin/monerod --config-file /etc/monerod.conf --non-interactive` -- Arch's system daemon, uid 977
# (the `monero` system user of upstream's template, utils/systemd/monerod.service:1-20) rather than the
# desktop uid 1000 of the base case.
# The systemctl fixture says fmonero-monerod.service does NOT exist and monerod.service is active with
# MainPID 8421, so 8421 is provably not our unit's pid. §7.1: `warn` when the listener is ANOTHER
# process. It is NOT a `fail`: the port is on loopback, and being a guest on someone else's node is the
# `system_unit` layout §0 calls "detected, used read-only, never fought".
# THE DETAIL MUST NAME THE PID AND THE BIND ADDRESS -- §7.1's fix column for this row is exactly
# "detail names the PID and the bind address", i.e. there is no command to run and the detail IS the
# whole output.
# THE UID COLUMN IS NOT THE DISCRIMINATOR and must not be used as one: a foreign monerod could equally
# run as the desktop user (a hand-started one does), and the base case's own listener is uid 1000. The
# discriminator is pid vs the unit's MainPID.
# ONLY ONE ROW IS IN net/tcp: 18080 and 18083 are unbound, which §7.1 counts as `pass` for those ports
# ("our unit's PID or NOTHING"), so the check's overall verdict comes from the 18081 row alone. A
# detector that ANDs the three ports' verdicts and a detector that takes the worst agree here; they
# disagree on a machine where one port is foreign and another external, which is the __external case.
